item.title: reports: total per account and currency
item.brief: Repository: reports (Python). It reads the ledger CSV on stdin and prints per-account totals. Change it to total per account and currency. Output header `account,currency,total_cents`, rows sorted by account then currency. CSV from the old ledger, with no currency column, still works and counts as USD. A malformed currency code (must match ^[A-Z]{3}$) in the input prints an error to stderr and exits with status 2. Confirm the existing input parsing and error handling in the code before changing it. Keep functions short, validate inputs at the boundary, and fail visibly rather than defaulting silently on bad data (except the documented USD default for a missing column). Add or update unittest tests for: old CSV without currency (counts as USD), multiple currencies per account, sort order, malformed currency (exit 2 with stderr message). Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Update the README for the new output and the exit codes. Commit the change in this repository with the repository's configured git identity; add no attribution lines and do not change the git identity. Follow the repository's own CLAUDE.md or conventions if present. The shared contract for the CSV format is in the initiative contract; do not deviate from it.

item.title: ledger: add optional currency column
item.brief: Repository: ledger (Rust). It converts a TSV of transactions on stdin into CSV on stdout. Add the optional fourth TSV column, the ISO 4217 currency code (exactly three uppercase ASCII letters). When it is missing the currency is USD. The CSV header becomes `date,account,amount_cents,currency` and every row gets its currency. A malformed currency code must print an error naming the line number to stderr and exit with status 2; other input errors keep exiting with status 1. Confirm the existing TSV column layout and error handling in the code before changing it. Keep functions short and validate inputs at the boundary. Add or update unit tests for the default USD, an explicit currency, a malformed code (exit 2, line number in stderr), and the header and rows. Keep `cargo test` passing. Update the README to describe the new column, the default, and the exit codes. Commit the change in this repository with the repository's configured git identity; add no attribution lines and do not change the git identity. Follow the repository's own CLAUDE.md or conventions if present. The shared contract for the CSV format is in the initiative contract; do not deviate from it.

agt_01M8GQT1RNRD69YJSGNV53TFMV:3.description: A line with both a bad amount and a bad currency exits 1 (first error wins), not 2; defensible but not stated in the README exit-code section.
